item.title: Show HN: An idle desktop incremental game driven by coding-agent
item.summary: While Codex or Claude is thinking or using tools, the game rains balls. As soon as the agent yields, new balls stop falling. I built it because I was bored of waiting during coding sessions—and I didn’t want to spend that time doomscrolling. The idea was inspired by a trip to Tokyo, where I saw people staring almost hypnotically at pachinko machines after work. I found it fascinating: something visually stimulating, interactive, and strangely relaxing, but with clear limitations. At first, the project was just a simple pachinko machine. Balls would drop whenever the game detected changes to the agent’s token file. Then I started adding more things to watch and interact with. Around the same time, I kept seeing news about layoffs related to AI. That gave me the idea for a satirical company-management game: AI agents work and generate balls, the balls hit workers, the workers lose bowls, and the company collects them.Utimately, the company only wants the bowls, the employees are just haversting machine.
